title: Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

reading.body:
A self-driving car operated by Avride struck and killed a duck in Austin, Texas, while operating in autonomous mode with a human safety operator present. The vehicle did not slow down or stop after hitting the animal. This represents a failure in perception or decision-making at the point of deployment, where the system did not detect an obstacle in its path or failed to take evasive action.

The presence of a human safety operator who also did not intervene suggests the system operated without effective human oversight during the incident. To catch this failure, the system would have required either better obstacle detection capabilities to identify the duck before impact, or a demonstrated protocol for the human operator to take control when hazards appear.

It is not established whether the duck's size, position, or behavior made detection infeasible for the system as deployed, or what specific gap in the vehicle's sensing or decision architecture led to the collision.

reports.title: A self-driving car in Texas hit and killed a mother duck, sparking neighborhood outrage
Residents say self-driving car killed duck in Mueller
Self-driving car runs over Mueller Lake Park duck, raising safety concerns
Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

summary:
An autonomous vehicle operated by Avride struck and killed a mother duck in the Mueller Lake neighborhood of Austin, Texas, prompting significant community backlash. The vehicle, which had a human safety operator present, did not slow down or stop after hitting the duck, according to a resident who posted about the incident on a neighborhood Facebook group. The duck had been nesting in a pot outside a local Italian restaurant, making it familiar to residents, which intensified their concerns about autonomous vehicle safety in their area.

Avride confirmed the vehicle was operating in autonomous mode at the time of the incident. The company investigated claims that the vehicle failed to stop at a stop sign and determined no such violation occurred. In response, Avride has adjusted its testing operations by excluding certain streets around Mueller Lake. The company is now evaluating potential technological improvements through simulations to help prevent similar situations in the future, though it has not paused autonomous vehicle testing entirely. Meanwhile, local residents have placed the duck's eggs in an incubator to preserve them.
